props.title: The size that fits the house.
props.lede: A holiday party at home is usually smaller than the host imagines, because the music has to fit where the party already is. These are the four sizes a house books in December, and any of them can be the whole night or one part of it.

rows.term: One guitar, or a singer with a guitar
rows.text: The size for an open house or a dinner for twelve. A jazz guitarist plays the Christmas book with the standards threaded through it, or a singer with a guitar plays the songs your guests ask for. Where the night will want a floor later, Tejas Singh plays the dinner on his own and the same booking grows to a quartet for the dancing.

rows.term: The Christmas jazz duo or trio
rows.text: Upright bass and guitar, with drums played with brushes when the party is bigger than a dinner, playing the Guaraldi record, the standards that are Christmas songs and the standards that aren’t. The balance of season to standards is yours, and the whole December book is on the Christmas jazz trio page.

A trio or a quartet playing the songs everyone in the house knows, for the part of the night when the furniture moves. Tony Medina plays it up to a four piece, and live band karaoke is the version where the band hands the microphone to whoever wants a song, on a big main floor or in a finished basement.
A DJ on their own, or after the band through the same sound system on the same contract, and the easiest late end a house can book. Band or DJ has its own post.

props.title: Three holiday parties a house throws.

rows.text: Neighbors, family and the people from work drifting in and out over an afternoon and an evening, so there are twelve people in the house at one point and sixty at another. A solo or a duo plays the season with the standards threaded through, so the people who stay all afternoon hear something new every hour.

One long table, or a few, and the meal is the point of the night. Upright bass and guitar play under it, the toast gets an announcement microphone, and a dinner for someone, a fortieth in December, gets its set built the way a milestone birthday does.

rows.term: The party that ends in dancing
rows.text: The cocktail party where the coffee table ends up in the hall and somebody’s aunt is the first one dancing. A trio or a quartet fills a main floor with no stage in it, plays dinner quietly first, and hands the late end to the DJ. It’s the one to book earliest.

props._notes:
The three holiday parties a house throws, each with the size that fits

props.title: The office parties book the December Saturdays first.
props.lede: In 2026 the December Saturdays before Christmas are the 5th, the 12th and the 19th, and every office party in the city wants the same three nights, decided between August and October. Peak weekends carry their own line on the quote, and a weeknight or a Sunday in December is the easier ask.

rows.text: Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, November 26 in 2026, and the week books two ways: the night before, when the house fills with people who flew in, and the Friendsgiving on the Saturday before or after. Both are dinners, so both book a solo or a duo playing the standards, with the season kept out of the set until you ask for it. The same size plays Christmas Eve and Christmas Day dinners.

New Year’s Eve is a Thursday in 2026, and it gets booked earlier than any other date of the season. At home it’s a trio or a quartet with the DJ through the same sound system, the countdown gets the announcement microphone, and the Christmas jazz trio plays it with the set turning from the season to the swing book as the night goes on.

Some houses skip December on purpose and throw the party in the second or third week of January, when nobody else wants the same Saturday. The January party post makes the case for the office version of the same move.

items.q: Can we book a band for a Christmas party at home?
items.a: Yes. A house books one guitarist or a singer with a guitar for an open house or a dinner, the Christmas jazz duo or trio for drinks and dinner, a party band for the part of the night when the furniture moves, and a DJ on its own or after the band. It's one contract with one personal contact, booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

items.q: Do you play Christmas music, or just the standards?
items.a: Both, and the balance is yours. The Christmas jazz trio draws on the Vince Guaraldi record from the Charlie Brown special, the standards that are Christmas songs, and the standards that aren't, threaded through so a three-hour party doesn't hear the same carols twice.

items.q: How loud is it in a house?
items.a: At dinner, about the level of the conversation around it, so nobody at the table raises their voice. A party band turns up once the furniture moves, and the loud part of a winter party is indoors anyway, which makes December the easy month for the neighbors. If your building or HOA has quiet hours in writing, give them to us at contract.

items.q: How much space does the band need in a house?
items.a: A solo or a DJ takes about 6 by 4 feet, a duo 8 by 6, a trio 12 by 8 and a quartet 14 by 10. Each wants one dedicated circuit that the oven and the coffee makers aren't on (the quartet and the karaoke four-piece want two). Setup runs 45 minutes for a solo or a DJ and an hour for a duo or a trio. The tree usually stands in the corner the band would take, so tell us which corner is ours, and tell us about the driveway or the alley for unloading.

items.q: Is a dinner for twelve big enough for live music?
items.a: Yes. A dinner for twelve books one guitarist or a singer with a guitar in a corner, and an open house books a duo that works whether twelve or sixty people are in the house at the time.
